decisions.executionNote: Begin right-hand side approach to the holder on the right; left arm stays clear. Gradually turn wrist inward while establishing elbow-up motion.
Turn the right gripper toward the holder and advance gradually from the right side, keeping left arm parked.
Replan from observed wrist after continuity interruption. Use smaller motions to center open right jaws around holder sides and level the wrist.
Right wrist is near its rotation limit and holder shifted. Back off yaw while moving gently inward/down to reach a feasible side grasp.
Rejected chunk moved nothing. Attempt a very small upward and yaw-back retreat from the wrist limit before reapproaching.
Approach shifted holder center with open right jaws; reduce wrist roll and remain off the rotation limit.
Close right jaws around the holder at the current side alignment, then make a small test lift. Retention must be checked visually.
The closed jaws appear above the holder rather than retaining it. Reopen and lower the side grasp to the holder body before trying again.
Stop the descent at the observed pose, close on the holder upper body, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Holder has not followed the lift. Advance open jaws farther onto its body and level the jaw plane; previous grip was too shallow at the rim.
Close at the deeper side alignment and test a 3 cm lift, checking whether the holder stays between the jaws.
Holder still rests on the table. Recenter the open grasp farther forward and lower toward its side, avoiding the near rim.
Lower the now-centered jaws onto the holder body and close without lifting yet.
Test a steady holder lift while beginning a gradual left-wrist downward approach toward the pens. Keep the right grip closed.
Holder follows the right hand in RGB. Maintain its grip while moving the left hand above the cyan pen and turning the jaws toward a top-down grasp.
Align left jaws across the cyan pen and descend slowly toward its upper body; hold the raised holder stationary in the right hand.
Fine-center the cyan pen between the left jaws, lower the final few centimeters, then close. Right hand continues holding the holder.
Maintain closure on the cyan pen and lift clear of the table to verify retention before reorienting it toward the held holder.
Cyan pen is retained. Lift and rotate it toward upright, moving both held objects nearer the center without crossing the arms.
Finish turning the cyan pen upright and approach above the held opening. Keep enough height for the pen's lower end to clear the rim.
Lower the upright cyan pen into the holder with a small centering correction. Hold the holder steady and keep both grips closed until the pen is inside.
Make a small inward correction, release the cyan pen into the opening, and withdraw the left jaws upward and left to verify insertion.
The cyan pen appears at the near rim rather than clearly seated. Regrasp gently and shift it slightly rearward over the opening before releasing again.
Guide the cyan pen's lower end into the visible opening, release it, and withdraw the open left hand while the right hand stabilizes the holder.
Cyan pen now appears seated in the holder. Clear the opening and begin rotating the left hand for a top-down grasp of the purple pen.
The previous turn was rejected without motion. Reduce rotation increments and retreat left at constant height to preserve joint continuity.
Move toward the purple pen while gradually pitching the left gripper downward, keeping the held holder stationary.
Finish the top-down alignment above the purple pen and approach to a short hover before the final grasp descent.
Lower the left jaws onto the purple pen with a small planar correction, then close while keeping the right-hand holder steady.
Lift the purple pen clear and begin turning it upright while moving slightly left to avoid the holder rim.
Purple retention is uncertain and it appears to be slipping below the jaws. Reopen and return to a safe top-down hover to reacquire it from its observed location.
Reorient the left jaws across the purple pen's new table direction and descend to a hover over its body. Holder remains stabilized.
Center the purple body, descend fully to the tabletop grasp height, and close the left jaws before any lift.
Allow the left jaws to finish closing, then make a straight test lift of the purple pen without changing its orientation.
The purple pen appears between the closed jaws. Lift higher and turn it toward vertical, keeping the holder steady and leaving clearance above the rim.
Raise the purple pen away from the rim and finish the upright wrist orientation before refining the insertion alignment.
Purple slipped and is back on the table. Move the holder farther right for clearance and return the open left hand toward a top-down reacquisition.
Align the open left hand over the relocated purple pen with the holder now clear to the right; continue a controlled top-down approach.
Correct the purple pen centering and complete a vertical body grasp, with extra closure dwell before lifting.
Keep the purple grasp fully closed and lift vertically clear, with a small retreat from the holder before reorientation.
Purple now follows the left hand. Raise it well above the holder and turn slowly while staying clear of the rim.
Complete the purple pen's vertical orientation high above the holder and bring the held opening beneath it without crossing the arms.
Lower the retained purple pen toward the empty side of the opening, leaving space beside the cyan pen. Keep both grasps closed until the lower end is inside.
Seat the purple lower end a little deeper, open the left jaws, and withdraw up-left while the right hand holds the holder.
Both colored pens remain inside the holder. Retreat left and turn toward a top-down grasp of the black pen; right grip stays closed.
Replan after the continuity interruption with smaller left-wrist pitch increments and a gradual retreat toward the black pen.
Approach the black pen in the left workspace, aligning the downward jaws across its shaft while keeping the filled holder raised.
Finish leveling the downward grasp and center over the black pen's body, descending to a short hover before closure.
Fine-center the black shaft, descend to its thin tabletop profile, and close the left jaws with a short dwell before lifting.
Maintain the black-pen closure and lift straight clear of the table before reorientation; verify retention visually.
Black pen follows the closed left gripper. Lift higher and gradually turn it upright while approaching the holder from the left.
Finish turning the retained black pen upright above the holder, staying high until its lower end is aligned with the remaining opening.
Guide the upright black pen downward into the free left side of the opening, with a small rearward centering correction.
Seat the black pen slightly farther inside, release it, then withdraw the open left jaws up and left while the holder remains supported.
Three pens are visible in the holder. Begin a gradual left-side approach to the remaining gold-and-black pen, preserving wrist continuity.
Move above the remaining gold pen and turn the open jaws downward across its shaft, keeping the supported holder stationary.
Replan from the interrupted approach: lower with smaller pitch increments and only a slight forward correction, avoiding the shoulder limit while aligning the gold pen.
Correct the remaining pen's lateral alignment using the wrist and head views, finish the shallow descent, and close around the shaft.
The forward approach reached an IK boundary. Retract the wrist slightly and tilt the fingers forward to reach the gold shaft without extending the arm farther.
Use the newly available wrist posture to make a small forward and left centering correction on the gold shaft, descend slightly, then close.
The gold pen is still outside the closed jaws. Reopen, shift the grasp forward toward the visible shaft, and close again without lifting.
The gold pen has been pushed rather than retained. Reopen and rise clear, shifting left over the shaft's middle before another descent.
Tilt the open fingers farther toward the gold shaft while descending, rather than pushing the wrist forward into the reach boundary.
Use the wrist view to move the open jaw center toward the gold shaft, with a small lift to avoid pushing it along the tabletop.
Gold shaft is now centered in the wrist view. Make a shallow final descent and close with a pause before the retention test.
Keep the gold-pen grip closed and lift while retreating from the far reach boundary. Check that the shaft follows before rotating it.
The gold pen follows the left hand. Raise it clear and gradually turn it upright while moving toward the supported holder.
Complete the gold pen's upright orientation while approaching above the holder, keeping both grips closed and the lower end above the rim.
Lower the upright gold pen into the remaining left-side space with a small lateral correction, keeping the holder supported.
Gold lower end appears near the left rim. Ease it inward and slightly forward, then lower gently rather than forcing against the existing pens.
Seat the gold pen farther inside the remaining space, open the left jaws, and withdraw up-left while keeping the holder supported.
Gold pen is leaning across the rim. Clear the open left jaws and pause briefly to see whether its lower end settles inside; keep the holder steady.
Gold pen is not seated and is slipping outside. Keep the holder stable and clear the left hand to observe its resting position for recovery.
Recover the gold pen from its new nearby table position. Begin turning the left jaws to match its reversed direction while staying above it.
Continue the gradual wrist turn above the gold pen, centering over its body before descending.
Finish the downward alignment over the relocated gold pen and descend to a hover above the shaft, with the holder held steady.
Fine-center on the gold shaft and descend to a thin-pen grasp height. Close and dwell without rotating near the wrist limit.
